diffs.diff: header pin 5: part says RXD, datasheet reading says RX
diffs.evidence: Winsen MH-Z14A manual, section 6 'Definition for pins': '11, 14,18,24  UART（RXD） TTL data input'; terminal connector pad 24 is RXD (sensor's data input). 'RX' is the same signal under a shorter name; the part's RXD (fn uart.rx, wire to MCU TX) matches the datasheet name exactly. Manual also says: 'Connect module's Vin-GND-RXD-TXD to users' 5V-GND-TXD-RXD.'

diffs.diff: header pin 6: part says TXD, datasheet reading says TX
diffs.evidence: Winsen MH-Z14A manual, section 6 'Definition for pins': '10,13,19,25  UART（TXD）TTL data output'; terminal connector pad 25 is TXD (sensor's data output). 'TX' is an equivalent short name; the part uses the datasheet's exact name TXD (fn uart.tx, wire to MCU RX).

diffs.diff: co2_ppm: datasheet reading gives 1 per count, the part's model has none
diffs.evidence: Manual, 0x86 return value: 'CO2 concentration = HIGH * 256 + LOW', example 'FF 86 02 20 ... 58' -> '2*256+32=544ppm', i.e. 1 ppm per count of the 16-bit big-endian value. The model already encodes exactly this: sim.uartReplies bytes [0xFF, 0x86, {control:'value', bits:16, scale:1}, 0 x32 bits, mhz19 checksum] and the driver returns buf[2]*256+buf[3]. The publish gate only reads conversions from sim.measure/measures/responses, not sim.uartReplies, so it reports 'none' although the scale is 1 ppm/count.
